[{"review_text": "This is the type of game that has a yearly release, similar to other sports game (apart from last year of course). That means gradual improvements, maybe not huge change year on year, but definitely noticeable over time and incrementally better. This was the year that was supposed to be the huge leap forward, with a brand new graphics engine and UI

Now you have to understand, Football Manager is not your typical game. 80% of its gameplay is essentially staring at spreadsheet for hours and hours whilst playing something in the background. Most of your playerbase spends hundreds if not thoudsands of hours in this game, and that is across multiple editions. So when your core audience has thoudsands of hours spent looking at spreadsheets a certain way, it is always going to be a huge risk reworking your game's entire UI. You have to be extremely careful and build it extremely well if you're going to do that. What SI did, is not even close. Not even a little bit.

Let's look at this FM edition as The New, The Old, and the Gone. 

[[The new]] 
[Positives]
- New tactics system - great, long time coming
- New graphics engine - compared to previous FMs? it's good, a big jump forward that leaves the door open for a lot of big improvements in the future. Compared to your average game? Looks like a 2012 game
- Some tiny changes like the mentoring screen

[Negatives]
- The entire UI and UX. The entire game has been redesigned from the ground up, and it's bad. There is one thing to force people to forget their muscle memory to learn something better and another to make everything a worse experience. Menus are hidden, screens are hidden, navigation is not intuitive, features are barebones, there are essential things missing, etc. 
-- The UI is clearly made with console first in mind
-- The UI is not scaleable. It looks the same on a small screen as it does on a wide monitor. It's very difficult to look at on a larger screen.
-- Key UX principles have been ignored when building this game. There are popups in popups in popups. There are screens with 3 bits of information that you need to click inside a popup to view. 
-- Key UI principles are out the window. Everything has thick borders. Things that are not clickable have borders. There are lists of 20+ items that each have borders on them to click on. It's visual overload and it makes people's heads dizzy
-- Functional bugs - the entire game is buggy. From obscure transfer history screens, to features completely not working, to 
 the game freezing at half time. Breadcrumbs don't work. Back button sometimes works ,sometimes doesn't, sometimes it takes you to a random place. Menus don't take you where you're supposed to go. Back arrows reset everything you filtered before and move you to the top of the screen even if you scrolled 40 entries down
-- Visual bugs - the game is INCREDIBLY unpolished. There are basic ui bugs like text cutting off, there are average UI bugs like dropdowns, checkboxes and radio buttons looking from a completely different game, and there are huge UI bugs like screens just not working properly. About 80% of the screens look like they were not fully polished
-- The speed - the game UI is incredibly slow. If you're going to put every bit of information behind minimum 3 clicks and 3 popups, it should be LIGHTNING fast. It's currently slower than a chrome tab on a Windows Pentium.
-- The flickers - every screen, menu and interaction is flickery when you go in an out
-- The rendering - the UI just looks weird, some elements are blurry and don't look HD, while others look very sharp and pixely, like they are not rendered properly.
-- The ballon d'Or winners are bugged
-- I can go on forever

[[The old]] 
Now let's talk about the old - aka what was already in there. Believe it or not, aside from the two bits under positive (graphics engine and tactics), all of that UI talk is just covering a new wrapper of the EXACT.SAME.GAME. 
Exactly, under the new UI and two new features, the game is absolutely the same game that was FM24. 
All of the core gameplay features have remained completely unchanged. Player interactions, transfers AI, contract negotiations, signing staff, manager movements, league and game sim AI, transfer logic, transfer and contract values, player development, training, etc. It's all the exact same and has seen no improvements. 
So what we're looking at in FM26 is spending tens if not hunderds of hours trying to adjust to a new UI in order to play the exact same game outside the matches. 

[[The gone]]
Finally, let's look at what's not here anymore. SI have announced that a bunch of features will be gone from FM26 (like international management, touchline shouts) and people have debated that enough. What they haven't announced though, is the countless of other features that they removed without notice. There are lists of tens of features completely or partially gone under the hood. Maybe not many huge ones, but a big part of quality of life. And as this game is played 80% outside the match day, these add up a lot. 
-- Data has been reduced to a minimum. Passmaps and heatmaps are gone from the game and the deep stats are barely there anymore
-- Records and history of leagues, players and best XIs are gone
-- Training is worse on all aspects
-- Staff management is worse
-- Youth team and player development is almost non existent
-- Navigating the world is a lot worse
-- The feeling of immersion is gone, as the "around the world" and "leagues in focus" sections are basically gone. You also don't get your shortlist's news tab anymore so good luck keeping track of staff or players at other clubs.
-- The world feels smaller

A lot of people have said this before and I really tend to agree - They decided to shift direction in order to appeal to more casual "fifa career mode" fans by simplifying every aspect of the game and dumbing down the part that happens between the matches.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 3, "timestamp_created": 1762332244}, {"review_text": "I have already close to 60 hours in this latest iteration of my favorite series, and unfortunately, I have mixed feelings. Setting aside the obvious (but aggravating) bugs and other technical issues, as they will most likely be addressed in updates and hotfixes, I think FM 26 simply wasn't ambitious enough in the right places. It does, however, succeed in the promised tactical innovations.

Where it was ambitious but fell short - the UI: The UI overhaul certainly is visually impressive at first glance but really creates a clunky experience when playing the game and navigating through different menus and pages. SI have attributed this to a need for hardcore FM players like myself to "unlearn" what we knew before, but I believe it is more down to poor design choices. It simply is not intuitive in many places. In others, it feels awkward because it was clearly designed to cater to console players.

Where it was ambitious and succeeded - tactics: The tactics overhaul in this iteration of FM has truly been fantastic to tinker with. I have always enjoyed the tactical side of the game, and FM 26 has introduced a new level of freedom to tactical-minded managers. While some of the player position terminology is a bit clunky (still better than the outdated terms used before), the overall tactical enhancements are clear. What is more, the game itself seems to respond to a larger variety of tactical choices when compared to previous FM games. In my season-long Braga save, I qualified for the Champion's League using a conservative mid-block approach paired with shorter passing and a lower tempo. In past iterations of FM, it was often difficult to avoid switching to a high pressing, high tempo tactical approach when in poor form. I also briefly tested a defensively solid counter-attack approach with Nottingham Forest, with moderate success.  I do think the only thing holding back these tactical innovations is the UI, which makes messing with tactics at best, awkward and at worst, frustrating. 

Where it was not ambitious enough - the game itself: Aside from the UI and the visual "coat of paint," this is still the same FM we've been getting for years. While, for some, this could be perceived as a positive, I think after waiting two years, I am disappointed with the lack of innovation here. Yes, there are new animations, like players looking up before driving a low cross into the box for a poaching striker to pounce on, but the actual core experience has not changed. In many cases, issues that the FM community have had with the game for over a decade are still present. Players will demand insane wages from you before signing for a team with less standing for lower wages and lower playing time. 

Where its ambition was oversold - the graphical enhancements: While I have never played Football Manager for the graphics or visual experience, I do think SI oversold this aspect of FM 26. It looks... fine. The most notable improvements are to non-human objects, like trophies, balls, etc. However, the in-game character models are still well over a decade behind other titles. For years, FM players have complained about the strange and unrealistic newgen (players generated by the game) faces. This is still a glaring issue here. I believe the improved and far more varied animations I mentioned previously mask many of the issues with graphical fidelity, making a match feel more "real" when watching it unfold from afar.

Conclusions: I am leaving this somewhat negative review out of a sense of duty to the FM community rather than to dog-pile criticism on SI. I genuinely love these games and only share my criticisms to offer constructive criticism as a hardcore player.  I only hope that SI takes the FM community's thoughts into account moving forward as they continue updating FM 26 and producing future titles. Long live Football Manager.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 2, "timestamp_created": 1762272172}, {"review_text": "Title: 25 Years of Loyalty Gone: FM26 is a UI Nightmare and a Beta Product in Disguise

Rating: 1/5 Stars

I have been managing virtual clubs since the days of Championship Manager 01/02. I’ve stuck with this franchise through most of my life that I have been playing games. But Football Manager 2026 is arguably the worst entry I have ever played, and for the first time in two decades, I’m uninstalling before the next game and reverting back to the old one, FM24.

As a professional UX/UI Designer, I look at interfaces for a living. The overhaul in FM26 is a textbook example of fixing what wasn't broken. The move to the Unity engine was promised as a revolution; instead, it feels like a regression.

Good design dictates that you don't alter User Experience (UX) just to freshen up the User Interface (UI). Yet, SI has done exactly that. They have buried critical information behind unnecessary clicks and flashy, tile-based menus that waste screen real estate. The data density, the very heart of a spreadsheet simulator like FM, has been sacrificed for a "modern" look that serves no function. It’s change for the sake of change, ignoring the muscle memory and workflow built by your core user base over twenty years.

A Beta Sold as a Full Release We were sold a brand new era of Football Manager. What we received is, at best, a glorified Beta. The game is incredibly buggy, with menu lags, visual glitches, and crash-dumps that break any sense of immersion. The "living, breathing world" feels sterile and disconnected compared to previous iterations. It’s hard to get lost in a save when you are constantly fighting the interface just to make a substitution or check a scout report.

The Verdict I am not against innovation, but I am against bad design. The UI could have been modernized without gutting the usability that made the series great.

I will be uninstalling FM26 and reverting to FM24. I won't be spending another penny on this franchise until I see a product that respects its users' time and intelligence. If you are a long-time fan, save your money. This isn't the revolution we were promised; it’s a ruin.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 4, "timestamp_created": 1764162917}, {"review_text": "Just play FM24 with mods. I genuinely have no idea how a game studio that makes a game with 20 million players could be so incompetent as to release THIS game after 5(!) years of development in the Unity Engine. Sports Interactive's PR team (read: half of youtubers) will say "uhhhh buddy have you heard of a BETA???? It's a frickin BETA there's gonna be BUGS. It's in a NEW ENGINE are you a PROGRAMMER??? Do you know moving to a new engine is HARD? Umm actually only 10% of the playerbase uses that feature so it's totally reasonable to REMOVE IT even though it was in the game since championship manager 94!!!" Don't listen to these people- this game is fundamentally broken on so many levels and it's unacceptable to increase the price to AAA pricing in a year where you brick it this hard on release. There are a few positives that can be taken from this game- but you won't be able to enjoy them until probably FM28, when SI are finally able to release a functional game. Since other members of SI's unpaid volunteer PR team have been saying "nobody can actually articulate what they dislike about the game! you're just afraid of change!" I'll list specifically everything I like and dislike about the game:

Like: 
- Potential for improved graphics/simulation/UI on Unity Engine
- The graphics ARE better, but they're now comparable to an early Wii game (generously). Great job SI!
- In and out of possession tactics are a great step forward for tactical flexibility and more control over your team's playing style. 
- Gegenpressing is less OP
- The UI looks more modern (in screenshots, before you actually use it)
- Premier League licensing

Dislike: 
- A million bugs  and crashes which you can read about on the SI forums. There are too many to list here.
- The UI is INCREDIBLY unresponsive. Yes, they added an option to make it snappier in exchange for waiting for tiles to load, but no game in 2025 should require you to choose between the two. 
- The UI is cluttered and unintuitive. Miles said to give it 20 hours before you judge it (LOL) and I have- it still sucks. It takes me several more clicks to reach the same screen as it did in FM24. I'm aware at this point where to find everything I'm looking for but it's just slower than FM24. They could've slapped a fresh coat of paint on FM24's UI and it would've been far better.
- Less robust data hub and in game data. There is much less information in the data hub for pre-match scouting than in FM24. In match, the most helpful data you can find is maybe xG or PPDA. In the "next opponent" scouting section, the game tells you their expected tactical setup. Great, they're playing a 4-2-3-1! Except the game doesn't tell you if they play with overlapping or inverted fullbacks, inverted or wide wingers, a false 9 or a poacher, etc so you effectively have no clue how the opposition will attack.
- Dribbling is broken. Your fullbacks will get rinsed by literally any winger.
- Players still won't square the ball. Match engine mods for FM24 dramatically improved this issue so I have no idea why SI still can't figure it out. 
- International Management removed from the game
- Game locked at 60 FPS. Maybe I wouldn't care if i was playing on a CRT TV, but it's 2025 and people are used to 144 hz monitors. There's really no excuse for this except that their game is so poorly optimized maybe they didn't want people to see the lag spikes that will ensue if you actually try to run it at higher FPS. 
- They INCREASED the price of the game in a year where they effectively released an alpha build of the game
- The new UI, graphics, and licensing are clearly meant to capture the attention of the drooling morons who still play fifa career mode. It won't work because fifa's graphics are still a million times better! SI are content to alienate their core playerbase in pursuit of people who will pick up the game, realize they can't hit the renegade with a facescanned Lamine Yamal, and never play again. 
- Newgen faces are still hilariously bad
- Apparently the in-game editor is unusable and they also increased the price of that!
- Every complaint from FM24 about reputation being broken, AI squad building, AI rotation, AI not playing youngsters, are still applicable.
- Players seem to disregard instructions like shoot less and work ball into box even more than last year.
- A million other things that I can't think of off the top of my head that you can find on the SI forums, reddit, or youtube.

All of the bugs might have been forgivable if the graphics or the UI were actually impressive- but the UI is a step backwards and the graphics have been upgraded to the point of only being 20 years out of date instead of 30. Maybe SI will fix the bugs, improve the performance, and reintegrate missing features before FM27 but until then this game is not worth purchasing.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 15, "timestamp_created": 1762736387}, {"review_text": "Very mixed feelings on this edition of FM. 

The negatives:
- The UI is bad. Is it as bad as everyone says? Maybe. As a UI designer myself, i can't help but have sympathy for the devs and designers challenged with conveying an Enormous amount of information and options at every given moment, and appreciate the plight of becoming so familiar with your own work in the design process that you become blind to the issue someone new will face. BUT, they literally had a template to work from which worked fine, and they chose to try and revolutionise it, and there is no arguments that this is an improvement. Every screen is overwhelming and unpleasant to look at. 
- In addition to the UI, the performance is Terrible. Again, I have sympathy for this, and it's often the case on the launch of a new product, but not one which has had years of work and should have had months of testing. There is barely a click made which doesn't cause the UI to flicker and jump and bug. There are graphical bugs present within the opening seconds of your experience - how was this not caught and addressed in literally the first round of testing? It makes the whole thing feel horrible to use, even on a decent computer. 
- Something i've not heard mentioned is the amount of small QOL options they've removed, too. Old games allowed you to customise small things like attribute thresholds and colours, which is now gone. Such a tiny thing, but a massive disappointment for me, as i find the colour options available horrible. 

The neutral:
- Player roles - largely good, but a couple of key roles removed which i've struggled to recreate with the new options. My favourite role was a Regista, but all three of the limited CDM options available have a fixed restriction on positional freedom. I don't understand why we have to be limited to existing roles, anyway? Why is there not just blank template roles for each position wherein i have to decide every trait of their performance? If I want a CDM who roams free, drifts to the wing, dribbles lots and shoots, then let me do it! Let me concede 5 goals a game and let it be my fault! Don't pen me into roles which the game has preprogrammed with only middling levels of customisation. 
- The camera angle. Personal problem, i know, but i hate how zoomed in it is by default. Yes, i can swap to another angle, but i also like the different angles the default camera brings. I genuinely like the graphical upgrade, this is just a tiny gripe as it can feel a bit claustrophobic. 
- The hair. Why has everyone got a mohawk now?


The good:
- The new tactics. I dislike the roles, but the in possession vs out possession structures is great, and completely changes my approach. I am still getting familiar with it, but i will be curious if it makes certain roles redundant (Why assign someone as an inverted wingback when I can have them play as a fullback out of possession and a CM in possession? May come to think i'm an idiot for that comment in time, but that's just how it's feeling right now!)
- The gameplay. It's not photorealistic, but it's a Huge step up. I thought 23 > 24 was an impressive jump, so this is an enormous leap in comparison. 


In summary:
It's not great, but it is an attempt at progress. You can argue all day whether they've targeted console gamers or watered things down or whatever, but there is no denying that we, like FIFA fans, have complained for years that they are effectively just giving us the same game year after year, and this year, it feels like they've tried something ambitious. They've messed it up, but they've tried something. 

All of us who have 3,000+ hours on each game get so familiar with the formula that you can play it with your eyes closed, whereas this feels like something we actually have to Play. 

Personally, i'm probably going to close it down and return to FM24 for a little while, until a few more updates are released, but i think there is the foundations of a promising future, provided they actually listen to the fans and really work on improving things.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 4, "timestamp_created": 1762595501}, {"review_text": "[h1]TL;DR - Should You Buy FM26?[/h1]

[b]Wait for FM27, updates or MODS.[/b] As a 25,000+ hour FM veteran, I cannot recommend FM26 in its current state. While the new tactical system is genuinely brilliant, the game is plagued by a catastrophic UI/UX downgrade, removal of 100+ features, and feels incomplete. Unless you're desperate for the new In/Out of Possession tactics, stick with FM24 or wait 6-12 months for patches.

[hr][/hr]

[h1]What's Actually Good[/h1]

[b]The New Tactical System (7/10):[/b]
[list]
[*]In/Out of Possession system is the best addition to FM in years
[*]Tactical visualizer is genuinely fantastic
[*]Much closer to mirroring real football than the old role system
[/list]

[b]Technical Performance (8/10):[/b]
[list]
[*]Unity engine brings massive speed improvements over FM24
[*]Loading times are excellent
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h1]What's Wrong - And It's A Lot[/h1]

[h2]The UI/UX Disaster (UI: 4/10 | UX: 1/10)[/h2]

[b]FM26 may have the worst UX downgrade in modern gaming history.[/b]

[b]Core Problems:[/b]
[list]
[*]Basic tasks require 3-5x more clicks than FM24
[*]Information buried behind multiple menus
[*]Zero customization options
[*]Fade transitions add annoying delays everywhere
[*]Search functionality barely works
[*]Almost no tooltips anywhere
[/list]

[b]Training Management - Catastrophic:[/b]
[list]
[*]Each training block requires separate setup
[*]Cannot copy/paste sessions
[*]U21/U18 training completely removed
[*]Out of Possession training doesn't work
[/list]

[b]Match Overview - Worse Than 10 Years Ago:[/b]
[list]
[*]Quick subs removed
[*]Cannot show heat maps or pass maps
[*]Cannot pause to analyze statistics
[/list]

[h2]Missing & Removed Features - Over 100+[/h2]

[b]Data & Analysis:[/b]
[list]
[*]❌ Heat maps removed
[*]❌ Pass maps removed
[*]❌ Cannot export data
[*]❌ Development Centre gutted
[/list]

[b]Youth Team Management:[/b]
[list]
[*]❌ U21/U18 tactics not shown
[*]❌ U21/U18 training removed
[*]❌ U21/U18 coach assignments removed
[/list]

[b]Major Game Modes Removed:[/b]
[list]
[*]❌ International Management (returning in update)
[*]❌ Create-a-Club (FM27)
[*]❌ Challenge Mode (FM27/28)
[*]❌ Fantasy Draft
[*]❌ Touchline Shouts (permanently removed)
[/list]

[b]Customization (1/10):[/b]
[list]
[*]Cannot rearrange tiles
[*]Cannot change attribute colors
[*]Cannot import real manager photos
[*]Cannot customize hotkeys (20+ years!)
[/list]

[h2]Match Engine - Same Old With New Paint[/h2]

[b]Critical Issues:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Referee actions broken:[/b] Cards appear BEFORE referee reaches for pocket
[*][b]Player marking broken:[/b] Becomes zonal marking inconsistently
[*][b]Visual clarity poor:[/b] Feels like watching 720p on 1440p monitor
[*][b]AI unchanged:[/b] Doesn't seem smarter than FM24
[*][b]No collision detection:[/b] In a "new" 2025 engine
[/list]

[b]Other Problems:[/b]
[list]
[*]Off-ball movement feels mechanical
[*]Ball physics feel off
[*]Rain effects annoying (always rains)
[*]Player models lack variety
[*]Out of Possession instructions don't work properly
[*]Mid-game tactical changes take 5-15 seconds
[/list]

[h2]Bugs From Beta[/h2]
[list]
[*]7 crashes from obscure UI elements
[*]Squad bar resets between matches (15+ years unfixed)
[*]Generated player faces look nightmarish
[*]Hitting woodwork 3+ times per match
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h1]Design Philosophy Concerns[/h1]

[olist]
[*][b]Console-First Development:[/b] PC playerbase didn't ask for this UI overhaul
[*][b]Solving Non-Problems:[/b] Creating many new problems
[*][b]Removing Features:[/b] 100+ beloved features removed
[*][b]2015 Standards in 2025:[/b] Unity used for 2015-level graphics
[*][b]Lack of Competition:[/b] Complacency is obvious
[/olist]

[b]Miles Jacobson's Quote:[/b] [i]"You can't expect 20 years worth of quality of life features from a UI to be there in a brand new UI."[/i]

Translation: They removed 20 years of features and you'll wait years for them to come back - maybe.

[hr][/hr]

Thank you Sports Interactive for finally making a game so bad that my obsession is over.

You'd be better off picking up FM24 for pennies and getting the game updates to get current squads.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 36, "timestamp_created": 1762347191}, {"review_text": "Not Recommended

After two years of waiting, this is honestly one of the most disappointing Football Manager releases ever. FM26 was supposed to be the big leap forward — new engine, new UI, new everything. Instead, it feels like a downgrade in every possible way.

The interface is a complete disaster. Everything that used to take one click now takes three or four. Menus are hidden behind layers of popups, navigation is confusing, and nothing scales properly on big screens. The back button randomly stops working, filters reset for no reason, and the game constantly flickers and lags when switching screens. It genuinely feels unfinished and painful to use.

Performance is terrible — slow, clunky, and full of bugs. Text gets cut off, buttons glitch out, and half of the UI looks like it was thrown together at the last minute. After two full years of development, this level of quality is just unacceptable.

Worse yet, it’s clear the developers don’t care about the core audience anymore. Features have been removed, stats simplified, and everything outside of matchday feels dumbed down. It’s hard not to feel like this release was made just to sell another version, not to improve the game.

I’m going back to FM24 — at least it works and makes sense. FM26 is simply a reflection of modern gaming: quick cash grabs over real progress.

I won’t be buying another FM for at least the next five years, or until this series gets back on track.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 0, "timestamp_created": 1762447152}, {"review_text": "the game is in a early development stage (lots of bugs and missing features) and is being sold as a fully developed product", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 2, "timestamp_created": 1762372042}, {"review_text": "Well... Waited 2 years for a game, that is still not finished, even on release day. 

[b]So many problems but here are a few :[/b]

- new UI with lots of widgets, you have to click a lot more to get the infos that you need. Everything is separated into smaller widgets, when everything could have been on one screen like before. It means 3 or 4 times more clicks, for one task.
- Simplification of interface feels like it's intended for beginners who don't want to get to a deeper level.
- Frequent bugs, technical issues (set pieces not saving and unable to load during game, fonts, lines, previews not always working properly)
- Horrible training feature (No drag and drop, each segments need to be opened individually)
- Missing options (saving squad, copy/past training, can't organize friendlies for reserve/U18, no drag and drop, no CTRL+A, etc)
- No option for modders to make skins (apart from changing colors here and there in the SI folder)
- Changing the staff stats from number attributes to text (Good, Very Good, etc instead of 0-20) and horrific staff coaching interface
- Women's leagues unbalanced (5-10 mill. in debt after 1 season, no point in playing with newgens since half of the current players are at 150/160 capabilities)

Feels like they wanted to do something so new and different that they left out the things that were most liked by the players. The game can be good for an audience that wants to play 1 or 2 seasons, recruits a few players and mostly clicks on "continue" and "next game", but in this state, you are not going to be able to play 1000+ hours because of how stupid and nerve wracking some features are.

Don't get me wrong, usually, change is good, but not here. if you change something, do it because you want to improve the gameplay experience. In this case, it feels like they just wanted to say "Look at all the things we've changed in 2 years, it's a whole new game", even if the experience is worse.

Some mods/skins/features made by the community are starting to emerge, making the experience easier and faster, but we cannot rely solely on them to make the game good. It shouldn't be their job to improve the speed of UI, adding x1,5 speed to games or patching newgen's faces...

[b]"Do you recommend this game?" At the moment no.[/b] It will be better in the future, bugs will be fixed, features will be added. Hopefully Sports Interactive has seen from all the reviews what people really want and they will surely act upon it. We all know that FM has great potential, but we will have to wait for it. Don't play it now and get disgusted, wait some time so you can fully enjoy it without encountering infuriating problems!", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 0, "timestamp_created": 1762275230}, {"review_text": "You've always bought FM. It's your game. You buy it every year because you can sink hours into it. You've heard about some issues with this one. You're on the fence. Kevin Toms was my first football manager game in the 80s. I am easy to please. I've got so many versions of FM in my steam library that I would have a hard time convincing anyone that it's a normal thing to buy it every year. Do yourself a favour. Skip this one. Bugs and lag. That's what you're buying. Bugs and lag.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 1, "timestamp_created": 1762417829}, {"review_text": "I can't believe I'm actually doing this, as an avid player of Champ Man and Football Manager games for over 30 years, I have very rarely been so disappointed.

I strongly recommend against buying this game. In some people's eyes the graphics of the match is everything and I can see some improvements in this area of this release, but if you're a detail, hardcore player who loves to get hands on trawling through many of the managerial tasks behind the scenes like me, then I fear you will be very disappointed.

The detailed, in-match tablet of stats is nothing like it used to be, and also no ability to make "shouts" from the touchline.

Away from the match engine the UI is not for me. I'm a PC/Laptop player (who uses a mouse), and I feel the change is awful. It's clunky and far more unmanageable, as are the views within various menus. So many useful things have just gone. No tool tips any more, it's such a waste.

If this is the best state of the latest version of the Football Manager game it makes me wonder what the hell has been going on for two years, and what the hell of a mess FM 25 must've been. 

I've stopped short of asking for a refund on this, mainly because I feel I've had more than my money is worth over all the years of play on FM, but honestly I expected far better than this product.

I'm sorry but at nearly £50, this is really not worth it.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 1, "timestamp_created": 1762529331}, {"review_text": "The game is a total mess. They capped the FPS at 30 and 60, the UI looks like something straight out of a mobile game and it’s exhausting to look at. There are countless bugs progression issues, matches freezing while players keep moving, visual glitches, even players wearing the wrong team kits. Places you could reach in 2–3 clicks before now take 7–8, and you call that “innovation.” No, it’s plain nonsense.

If you play in the Turkish league, you might come across a third-division-level player who feels like a “mentally nerfed Kevin De Bruyne” or “Ederson’s turtle version.” Researchers say they’re not doing it for money okay, Okay, but who’s to say there isn’t some kind of bias or outside influence when these player profiles are made? It really makes you wonder if that’s why some of these ratings feel so off.

And seriously what do you expect from a simulation game? Detail, obviously. But what do we get instead? This miserable excuse of a game that feels like a cheap mobile clone. You know those awful mobile football manager games with Mourinho on the cover? Yeah, it’s just as terrible as that.

There’s no match heat maps, no detailed post-match stats, no in-depth player interactions during games, no visual locker room scenes, no unique team talks, no option to send players to warm up (which could affect their performance or injury risk if you don’t), no variety in transfer negotiations, no training depth  absolutely nothing.

Two whole years and this is what they came up with. They’ve spent all that time trying to make a console-friendly product instead of an actual management simulation. Pathetic.

Balance is all over the place (maybe they’ll fix that in the February update, who knows). They even removed some of the features from FM24 that people actually liked.

As for the so-called “improved match engine and graphics” they’ve been hyping — it just looks like FM24 with extra brightness and saturation slapped on. (Yes, I’m playing on Ultra settings.)

There’s nothing here that players were expecting or anything that justifies waiting two full years. Overall, it’s a huge disappointment.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 3, "timestamp_created": 1762277883}, {"review_text": "A Heartbreaking Step Backwards 

I’ve been playing this series since Championship Manager 2. I’ve seen every evolution, every engine rewrite, every experiment, every stumble — but Football Manager 26 is the first time I’ve genuinely felt disappointed to the point of switching the game off and wondering how we got here.

The UI is nothing short of atrocious. Instead of quick, clean information, the screen is now an explosion of clunky pop-out boxes and layered menus that break the flow of management. Nothing feels intuitive, everything is nested or hidden, and what used to be a fast, immersive experience has turned into a constant battle just to navigate basic features. It feels like someone decided to redesign for the sake of it, rather than because it improved anything.

But the real gut-punch is the loss of immersion. We’ve gone from feeling like a manager pacing the technical area, barking touchline orders and adjusting tactics in the heat of the moment — to feeling like someone flicking through awkward UI tabs on a spreadsheet dressed up as a matchday. No quick tactical tweaks, no fluid decision-making, no connection to what’s actually happening on the pitch. Just hollow interaction where depth used to be.

This is, without exaggeration, the weakest entry the franchise has ever produced. Not because the idea of pushing things forward is wrong — innovation is healthy — but because so much of what already worked beautifully has been ripped out or buried beneath a clumsy interface. You shouldn’t fix what wasn’t broken, and FM26 is a perfect example of what happens when you do.

I never thought I’d say it after three decades with this series, but this release has genuinely made me step away and question whether the game I grew up loving is still there under all this UI clutter and removed immersion. Heartbreaking. Disappointing. Know what expansions you need to save yourself some money. Core free game is fast to level through, taking me roughly 3 days to hit max level. More casual players could easily still do it over the course of a week. Unfortunately there is a lot of prep work you need to do once you hit 80 before you can really start doing what you want, but once you get that out of the way the game really does open up unlike any other MMO with tons of options to do.

My opinion on expansions and their worth:

1. Heart of Thorns - Arguably the best maps and group content but otherwise only needed if the elite spec you want to play is locked behind it.

2. Path of Fire. - Required for the mounts and honestly unlocking them is really fun.

3. End of Dragons - If you skip Heart of Thorns then this is a must buy for the glider. You dont get the masteries but you don't need them. Jade bot is a nice extra. If you're tight on money choose this or Heart of Thorns depending on which elite specs you want access to.

4. Secrets of the Obscure - Potentially needed if the build you want to play requires the extra weapon unlocks. Great because it gives you access to a faster way to get the most important mount in the Skyscale. If you're okay with it taking way longer to get Skyscale and you don't need the extra weapon then skip.

[*][b]Cooperation isn't endorsed enough[/b]. [*][b]Monetization.[/b] No subscription means they still need to earn money somehow. So they'll sell you UI enhancements (extra inventory bags slots, storage space in the item bank etc), but also QoL things like revival potions and better harvesting tools, and premium flashy skins in the ingame shop - as well as extra story chapters. On the brighter side, game offers official way to exchange regular currency for premium and vice versa

[h3]Pros:[/h3]

[*][b]No pressure to play.[/b] No subscription means you never feel obligated to spend at least that much hours playing it. After you've got a fully-maxed character, it will only be different from those playing for 10 years in its looks, they won't get any mechanical edge over you, except for them having more experience and skill. - beim installieren des Spiels als Verzeichnis auswählen Steam\steamapps\common
- Steam öffnen, in Steam auf GW2 installieren klicken

- fertig, GW 2 über Steam spielen mit Spielzeit etc.
- für Veteranen (so hab ich es gemacht) Speil deinstallieren und oben genannten Schritt durchführen

"FREE TO PLAY":
Würde ich niemanden empfehlen. Das Spiel ist 10 Jahre alt und die Vanilla Version bietet zwar sehr sehr viele Stunden Spielspaß, aber ohne DLC hat man aktuell Einschränkungen (keine Reittiere etc.). Für 30 Euro sind die Erweiterungen Guild Wars 2:Heart of Thorns™ und Guild Wars 2: Path of Fire™ in meinen Augen Pflicht für den vollen Spielspaß.

SPIELZEIT:
Ich habe in Guild Wars 2 über 5000 Spielstunden, 9 Charaktere auf max Level. Komplettes legendäres Gear von Rüstungen und Waffen, alle Dlc's .... und ich habe trotzdem nicht alles erreicht, was möglich ist.

SCHWIRIGKEIT UND SPIELMODI
- "easy to learn, hard to master"
- einmal Gear auf lvl 80 und du kannst das ganze Spiel erleben. Es gibt keinen Gear grind loop.
- Zeit für max Gear (exotic Armor) ca. 3 Wochen Spielzeit, wenn überhaupt
- "Endgame Gear" z.B. legendäre Rüstung und Waffen oder auch die aufgestiegenen Sachen sind grindlastig mit minimalen besseren Stats als exotic Gear
- Fokus liegt absolut auf PVE open World, Casualspieler können im PVE 98% erleben ohne große Herausforderungen
- Dungeons, Fraktale, Raids benötigen Erfahrungen, können aber getrost ignoriert werden
-WvW (Welt gegen Welt) und PVP sind nicht der Fokus - ArenaNet selbst spricht davon, sich mehr auf PVE open World zu konzentrieren. Das merkt man letztendlich daran das WvW und PvP wenig Neuerungen erhalten. Wer eher Fokus auf PVP hat sollte die Finger von dem Spiel lassen.

KLASSEN UND KAMPFSYSTEM
- kein Klassensystem wie in herkömmlichen MMORPG
- Jede Klasse kann auf DPS gespielt werden
- einige Klassen sind besser im Support und Heal als andere
- Actionskills werden durch die Waffe bestimmt (EIne Axt gibt dem Krieger andere Skills als ein Großschwert)

- Skillungen können jederzeit for free umgeskillt werden
- Erweiterungen Guild Wars 2:Heart of Thorns™ , Path of Fire™ und End of Dragons™ bieten jeder Klasse neue Spezialisierungen, die sich komplett unterschiedlich spielen lassen (z.B: Nekromant mit Zweihandschwert auf Beschwörungen von Untoten oder mit Zepter auf Sandmagie zum heilen )
- insgesamt 9 Klassen (eine Klasse nur mit Erweiterung Guild Wars 2:Heart of Thorns™)
- 3 Stoffklassen, 3 Lederklassen, 3 schwere Rüstungsklassen

INGAMESHOP
Im Grunde kann man den getrost ignorieren. Ingamewährung kann im Spiel selber ohne Echtgeld erworben werden. Items im Shop sind zu 99,9% kosmetisch. Es gibt nur ca. 3 Items die einfach das leben erleichtern wie z.B. unendliche Werkzeuge und sowas, aber absolut kein muss.

LEVELSYSTEM
- Maximal Level ist 80, danach sammelt man Beherrschungspunkte ähnlich einem Paragonsystem aus Diablo
- jede Map hat ein Levelcap, soll heißen als LVL 80 werde ich im Anfangsgebiet auf LVL 5 runterskaliert, wodurch auch erfahrene Spieler in Low Level Gebieten unterwegs sind
- Itemloot ist immer persönlich, keiner "schnappt" sich da was weg

COMMUNITY
- eine der besten, liebenswertesten, hilfsbereitesten, anfängerfreundlichsten Communitys überhaupt
- in GUILD Wars kann man sich in Gilden zusammen schließen
- man kann in mehreren Gilden parallel sein

STORY
- durch das Alter des Spiels gigantisch, ich schätze die reine Storyzeit alleine auf über 1000 Spielstunden
- ACHTUNG: bestimmte Storyelemente waren nur zu bestimmten Zeiten verfügbar (Living Story). Diese Abschnitte sind hinter einer kleinen Paywall gelockt
- inhaltlich würde ich die Story in Standard MMORPG einstufen. Seichte Kost. Wer hier ein "Last of us" erwartet, wird enttäuscht
- neben der Story gibt es "unendlich" viel zu tun. Leider kann ich in dem Review nicht auf jeden Punkt eingehen sonst wird das hier eine Masterarbeit

WEITERE WICHTIGE PROS:
- Grafik ist für das Alter unwahrscheinlich gut
- Erweiterungen sind einmalige Kosten, die ich auf jeden Fall empfehle, zumindes die ersten beiden für 30 Euro
- Klassen, die man so noch nicht kannte (hast du schonmal einen Dieb gespielt mit Dolchen und Kurzbogen und dann umgeskillt auf Zepter mit Schattenmagie?) Mesmer, Ingenieur, Wiederkehrer
- mit Freunden jederzeit Serverübergreifend Spielen
- ich habe über 5000 Spielstunden und du fängst neu an? Spiel einfach 3 Wochen dann bist du genau so "stark" wie ich und kannst sofort mit mir alles mit machen. Uns unterscheidet nur die "Erfahrung"
- "Fashion Souls" - es gibt unglaublich viele Skins für Rüstungen und Waffen und alle (Selbst die Startkluft) schaut gut aus
- du bist dir unsicher? Dann einfach free to play runter laden und nach der Vanilla die DLC's kaufen

FAZIT:
Guild Wars war DAS Spiel meiner Kindheit. Mit Guild Wars 2 habe ich die letzten 10 Jahre sehr viel schöne Erfahrungen gesammelt und viele Spieler kennen gelernt. Der Umfang dieses Spiels ist gigantisch. Mein Gear hat sich seit 6 Jahren kaum verändert und ich schaffe jeden Content in dem Spiel. Es ist einsteiger freundlich und sehr gut geeignet für Veteranen wie mich, die auch mal eine Pause brauchen.

"MMOs may age, but Guild Wars 2 just gets better with time."

🧭 WHAT IS GUILD WARS 2?

Guild Wars 2 is a massively multiplayer online RPG (MMORPG) that breaks the mold of the genre. Instead of stale quests and endless grinding, it gives you dynamic events, fluid combat, and a world that lives and breathes around you.

Whether you’re a solo explorer, hardcore raider, roleplayer, or WvW commander — GW2 has something tailored to you. No subscription required. Just play, explore, and get lost in Tyria.

⚔️ COMBAT: FAST, FLUID, AND FUN

This isn’t tab-target snoozefest combat. GW2 delivers:

🔁 Active combat – dodge, reposition, interrupt, and combo your skills

🔥 Weapon-based skill sets – your weapon changes your skills, making class builds endlessly flexible

⚔️ Profession specializations – turn a Guardian into a firebrand, a Thief into a deadeye, a Ranger into a soulbeast — it’s deep and creative

🧠 No holy trinity – healing, tanking, and DPS are distributed across builds; it’s more about teamwork than fixed roles

Whether you're cleaving through mobs in an open-world meta or weaving clutch support heals in fractals, combat is engaging from level 1 to endgame.

🌍 THE WORLD OF TYRIA: VIBRANT, VAST, AND BEAUTIFULLY ALIVE

Tyria isn’t just a backdrop — it’s a living, breathing world:

🌎 Dynamic Events — Forget static quests. The world changes around you. Villages can fall, dragons can raze zones, and you can jump into massive world bosses like Tequatl or Shatterer without a party finder.

🧩 Map exploration is meaningful — every corner hides jumping puzzles, lore, breathtaking views, or a mischievous asura NPC

🎨 Art direction is stunning — from the glowing caverns of the Maguuma Jungle to the vast desert of Elona, the game still looks gorgeous in 2025

Exploration doesn’t feel like a chore. It’s the reward.

🔝 ENDGAME: CHOOSE YOUR DESTINY

🛡️ PvE: Strike Missions, Fractals (GW2’s version of mini-raids), 10-man Raids, and massive meta-event chains like Dragon’s End

⚔️ PvP: Structured, balanced 5v5 arenas where skill matters, not gear

🌐 WvW (World vs World): 3-server warfare with siege weapons, zergs, scouts, and epic tactical battles across giant maps

💎 Fashion Wars: Yes, this is a real endgame. Tons of dyeable, earnable, and transmutable gear with no cash-shop pressure.

There’s no subscription fee — you pay for expansions, and you get everything. No “pay to win”, no lootboxes full of power, just cosmetics and convenience items.

🧱 EXPANSIONS: MASSIVE, MEANINGFUL, AND WORTH IT

Each expansion adds a TON of content and new mechanics:

🌿 Heart of Thorns – vertical maps, gliding, elite specs

🏜️ Path of Fire – mounts (best in any MMO, period), desert maps, more elite specs

🐉 End of Dragons – fishing, skiffs, Jade bots, deep lore

🌊 Secrets of the Obscure – more aerial combat and open world revamps

⚔️ Upcoming expansions keep delivering every year now

Expansions aren’t just new maps — they shift how the game plays.

✅ PROS:

⚔️ Best combat in any traditional MMO

🧭 Truly rewarding exploration and dynamic world

👥 Massive player events that feel epic

🎮 No sub fee — buy once, play forever

💬 Super active devs and friendly community

🎨 Insane fashion potential (glamour game supreme)

❌ CONS:

🧭 Early leveling can feel directionless if you’re used to traditional questing

📜 The base game story pacing is slow (but improves dramatically with expansions)

🔀 So many build options it can be overwhelming (but there are great tools like MetaBattle)

🧃 The UI is functional but could use modernization in places

💬 VERDICT:

Guild Wars 2 isn’t just alive — it’s thriving. In a genre where too many MMOs feel like chores or gated theme parks, GW2 feels like a sandbox playground with purpose. You’re not just ticking boxes — you’re out there being a part of the world.

Whether you want to duel on cliffs, fish in crystal waters, conquer dragons with 80 strangers, or just vibe in Divinity’s Reach in your legendary armor, GW2 offers freedom, fun, and fantasy like no other.

⚔️💎 9.2/10 – A top-tier MMO without the chains. Play it your way — Tyria is waiting.

For the first two–three weeks, ARC Raiders was that rare case: a game about raids, atmosphere and survival.
Now most matches feel like an arena for aggressive streamer content (and other content creators), where a normal player is just expendable. 

· WHY I LIKED THIS GAME SO MUCH

Visually and atmospherically, ARC Raiders is honestly a piece of art.
Concrete brutalism that feels like a Soviet–era architecture fever dream, mixed with industrial aesthetics in the form of rusted structures; post–apoc–punk clothing with retro–futuristic elements that could be ripped straight out of old sci–fi – it all works together as one coherent style. 

The sky and distant vistas are the kind that make you want to just stand there and stare. 

Sound and audio design set the overall feeling of a raid and give that rare sense of: “I am actually in another world.” The developers themselves called audio one of their “strategic pillars”, and you can feel it: this is a game you first play with your ears, and only then with your eyes. 

The raid atmosphere and the map as a sandbox: tension and unpredictability, a world you genuinely want to explore, where every run can feel unique. All of that existed in the first phase of the game’s life (those early weeks) – the game really did deliver that experience, until it became flooded by mass PvP purely for content. 

· WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED

I want to freeze in time the moment when it was still possible to play ARC Raiders “normally”. For me, this was that rare case when a game actually gave me a feeling of happiness and deep engagement. ARC Raiders could easily have become one of those games I come back to for years. 

But right now it is being buried by one specific thing – an aggressive meta pushed by streamers. 

· HOW IT LOOKED BEFORE THE “EVENTS” 

Not that long ago, matches looked roughly like this: 

– you drop into a raid;
– sometimes you run into other squads;
– some players choose to interact, some choose to avoid you;
– there were tense moments (“is this guy a d***bag or actually a decent dude?”), but you did not have the feeling that every single person you met was a f***ing psycho sprinting at you and screaming for “content” on TTV or TikTok. 

You could:

– team up and destroy ARC machines together;
– loot buildings (there really is enough loot for everyone);
– help each other with quests;
– sometimes extract side by side with total strangers – and that felt great. 

Now it is a completely different story. 

· WHAT CHANGED

After one particular streamer (TheBurntPeanut) decided to start his “war” and hyped his audience into playing as aggressively as possible, this started: 

Every encounter = automatic KoS gameplay.
(For clarity: KoS = Kill On Sight.)
No attempt to communicate (I literally carry defibs just to pick random people up), no reading the situation – just instant deletion of anything that moves.
Or they hard–ignore you until you get knocked, then suddenly turn on their mic to brag about being from some “faction”. Bro, we are in solo. What f***ing faction are you talking about? 

Camping exits and key locations.
People sit on extracts and quest spots not for loot, but for “clean frags” for recordings or streams. And it is not even impressive – the shooting in this game is extremely simple; this is not CS or PUBG, where gun skill actually matters a lot more. 

Matches feel less like raids and more like BF/CoD with extraction sprinkled on top.
Instead of tense PvEvP, you get a pure PvP arena with some running to the exit. On top of that, depending on luck, the surrounding PvE can either screw you over or bail you out: bots aggro whoever they see first and often end up helping your enemy. 

Naturally, part of the community picked all this up: people watch how their favorite streamers or YouTubers play and simply copy the style. As a result, a normal player (or a newbie) who came for an extraction adventure, not for a never–ending circus of clips, just stops having fun. 

Friendly or neutral players slowly turn toxic too. As we all know, evil breeds evil: if you get ratted out ten times in a row, your hands start itching to play the same way. If it keeps going like that, we might as well rename the game to RAT Raiders. 

· WHY THIS IS NOT JUST A PROBLEM FOR “SNOWFLAKES”

I am not against PvP and I am not asking for some “hippie chill–only mode” (I can play aggressively – I just keep hoping the person in front of me will turn out to be reasonable, not an a***le). 

But right now: 

The game is losing its identity.
Instead of a unique mix of co–op raids and risky PvEvP, we are getting yet another simulator of “shoot everything you see” (well, except ARC, apparently). 

The experience is dictated not by design, but by streamers and their fanbases.
Today they feel like “playing like psychos” – and the whole server turns into a toxic festival of aggression, and everyone else is basically forced to live in that format. 

New players are thrown straight into the most toxic version of the game and make the only logical conclusion: this is just another toxic KoS trash pit – so they uninstall it, or in the worst case, go straight for a refund. 

· WHERE THE DEVS COME INTO THIS

The problem is not just one freak who started a “war for content”. The problem is that: 

The game has no tools to balance player behavior or dilute the total KoS clown meta:
no karma, no reputation, no rewards for helping others or for non–aggressive behavior, no real tools for peaceful interaction, no convenient signaling or identification systems, and so on. 

There is no clear stance.
Is this a game about raids, survival, adventure and destroying ARC –
or about “shoot everything that moves”? 

Right now it feels like the developers themselves have not fully decided what they want from their own creation, and that empty space has been filled by streamers. They are effectively the ones setting the tone. 

If you let streamers and content creators define the behavioral meta, be ready for your game to become a hostage to their moods. That is exactly what is happening right now. 

· WHAT I WOULD LIKE TO SEE

If the developers really want to keep ARC Raiders as an interesting extraction experience, and not just another PvP arena, we need at least some of this: 

– Systems that reward a variety of playstyles, not just brain–dead total KoS shooting.
Yes, technically something already exists (killing raiders gives less XP than killing ARC), but that is nowhere near enough. 

– Counter–measures against constant extract camping and stream–sniping for highlights.
Shoutout to that “Partisan” from EFT – at least there, there is a dedicated NPC whose whole job is to hunt down ratting campers. In ARC Raiders, there is not even a hint of that kind of counterweight to this playstyle. 

– A clear communication stance: what kind of game this actually is and what behavior is considered “normal”. 

– Basic boundaries for friendly play.
For example: if you signal “I am friendly”, get a clear “yes, me too” back, and then the guy just shoots you in the back – that should be reflected somehow: karma hits, reputation loss, something. And honest play, on the contrary, should be rewarded. 

You could even go for a more radical approach: put the “bad boys” in lobbies with other bad boys, and sane players with sane players, with some kind of redemption system if someone decides to start playing normally. The online population allows this – there are enough people to separate rats and normal players into different lobbies.

[h2]Arc Raiders Review[/h2]

[h1]Seems Like A Plausible Future[/h1]
Bro, just picture this: you’re part of a crew of scavengers, heading up to the surface of a post-apocalyptic world, guns in hand, adrenaline coursing, enemies all around both robotic and human. That’s literally the premise of ARC Raiders. It’s a third-person extraction shooter where you leave a safe base, enter a hazardous map, loot stuff, survive or die trying, and attempt to extract with what you found. It blends PvE (environment/AI) and PvP (other players) in a way that aims to keep things tense, unpredictable, and fun.

I jumped into ARC Raiders wanting high thrills and a solid extraction-shooter loop. What I found was a game that hits a surprising number of high notes, but also has a few rough edges. Let’s just jump into this long-ass review.

[h1]About This Game [/h1]

[h2]Storyline [/h2]
The story in ARC Raiders isn’t the typical cinematic blockbuster with shit ton of cutscenes, it’s more atmosphere, setting, and context than “here’s a hero’s journey”. The game is set in a distant future Earth where climate collapse and sinister machines (the “ARC” robots) took over the surface, forcing humanity to retreat underground into a settlement called Speranza. Raiders (that’s you) are volunteers (or daredevils) who go up to the surface (the “Topside”) to scavenge resources, weapons, relics…basically anything that can help humanity survive.

The tone is bleak, but with a sliver of hope. You’re fighting to stay alive, to get home, and maybe help rebuild something. It gives the extraction-loop more emotional weight; losing your loot or dying means more than just “I lost gear”; it means you failed humanity’s cause a little bit (in my mind anyway, I’m a bit delusional like that).

[h2]Gameplay Mechanics[/h2]
This is the meat of the review, because ARC Raiders shines (and sometimes struggles) in its systems. I’ll break this down into sections:

[h3]Extraction Loop[/h3]
At its core, you start in a safe base (underground), pick load-out/weapons/gadgets, then drop into a map (30-ish minutes typical) on the surface. You loot, complete objectives/quests, fight ARC robots, maybe other players, then try to extract alive with your spoils. If you die, you lose almost everything (Except the stuff you store in your Safe Pocket).

This loop brings tension, the “will I survive?” question looms large. When you do extract, it’s rewarding. When you fail…well, you feel it. But in my playtime I found the loop compelling. I found myself thinking “just one more run” more times than I expected.

[h3]Combat: PvE (Robots) & PvP (Players)[/h3]
[b]Robots & AI enemies:[/b] These are a big part of the tension. The ARC machines are smart-ish, varied, and dangerous. You’ll find standard drones, lots of smaller ones, and big hulking machines that punish sloppiness. The moment when you think “I’m safe” and then a drone breaks cover and stuns you? That punch hits. Combat against AI here is legitimately good.

[b]What’s more, the AI reacts:[/b] if you shoot off a rotor, a drone might spin out and crash. I really loved the physics finesse. I found this added depth: you aren’t always just trading bullets, you’re managing positioning, noise, cover, and timing.

[b]Player vs player:[/b] Here’s where the extraction genre cliché kicks in. Encounter another player or team and you immediately have to consider: friend? foe? ambush? The paranoia is real. Many moments I found myself sneaking, watching, deciding “do I engage or avoid?” The game doesn’t force you to kill every human you meet, and sometimes mutual avoidance is the smartest play.

[h3]Gear/Loot/Progression[/h3]
One frequent worry in extraction shooters is: “Do I lose everything and get wound back to zero?” ARC Raiders handles this with a more approachable progression. Most of the more powerful weapons are made for dealing high damage against the machines but would not completely overwhelm against humans. That means new players can feel they have a fighting chance.

Here are key elements:
[list]
[*][b]Looting:[/b] You pick up weapons, materials, gadgets, salvage inside a run. If you extract, you bring them back and can use them; if you die, you lose them (unless in a safe pocket maybe).
[*][b]Crafting/upgrading:[/b] Back in base you can turn materials into weapons, gadgets, armor, and upgrade your gear. This adds motivation and a sense of growth.
[*][b]Skills/Progression:[/b] There’s a skill tree. You earn XP if you extract and even if you don’t, you still get XP, so you’re always progressing in some way. This makes the genre more accessible.
[*][b]Risk vs reward:[/b] The loop of “loot something great, survive extraction, feel awesome” works very well. But because death can hit you hard, you come to respect caution.
[*][b]Balance:[/b] The game tries to avoid an unbeatable loot-gap where veterans always dominate newbies. I appreciated this, in my early plays I didn’t feel completely hopeless. Some better gear helps, but it doesn’t guarantee victory. To quote: “better guns are better, but it’s never the reason you win or lose a fight.”
[/list]

Here’s a quick table summarizing:
[table]
[tr]
	[th]Mechanic[/th]
	[th]My Impression[/th]
[/tr]
[tr]
	[td][b]Loot & Extraction[/b][/td]
	[td]Tense and satisfying when you succeed; thrilling to carry something out[/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
	[td][b]Gear progression[/b][/td]
	[td]Solid! Gives you something to work toward without punishing newcomers[/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
	[td][b]Skill tree & XP[/b][/td]
	[td]Good touch. Makes you feel you’re improving even in losses[/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
	[td][b]Balance between new & vet[/b][/td]
	[td]It felt fairer than many extraction shooters[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]

[h3]Quality-of-Life & Other Features[/h3]
The game doesn’t just stop at core loop; there are features that smooth things out:
[list]
[*] The game allows you to auto-unload your backpack after a match, reducing the “inventory drag” many extraction shooters have. 
[*] Tooltips explain what items do and where to find them which means less aimless looting. Good for less experienced players. 
[*] Solo matchmaking tends to match you with solo players, which helps balance.
[/list]
I liked these features, little things that make a big difference in my experience. It’s the kind of polish that shows the developers are thinking of more than just hardcore players.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

So, wrapping up. ARC Raiders is a standout in the extraction-shooter genre right now, blending high-tension action with smart AI, accessible progression, and emergent social dynamics. It gives you that “one more run” itch, which is a sign of something good.

It’s not perfect: extraction shooters are inherently volatile (you might lose a lot), and tech/bugs can get in the way. But those are trade-offs I’m willing to accept given how many high-quality moments I had.

From me, I’d recommend it if you:
[list]
[*] Want extraction-type gameplay (loot-then-extract)
[*] Don’t want to start at a complete disadvantage
[*] Are okay with the possibility of frustrating losses
[*] Enjoy co-op/solo multiplayer with tension and strategy
[/list]

If you don’t like losing gear, or you hate unpredictability, or you prefer story-heavy single-player experiences, you might skip this one or at least go in knowing what you’re getting.

In short, ARC Raiders gives me that punch of adrenaline, the variety of “what happens next” and the satisfaction of survival, and it does so in a way that feels fresh and approachable. So yeah…two thumbs up from me.

Rating 10/10

Mad respect.", "voted_up": true, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 1, "timestamp_created": 1758294714}, {"review_text": "Sadly I cannot recommend this game just yet. This game has a massive identity crisis and with current content it's essentially an extended demo.

First let me commend this game for what it does right:
- combat is fun and satisfying, both when flying the ship and when on foot, there's issues with it like scarse ammo, harder difficulties throwing obscene amounts of enemies at you from buggy spawn points and heavy weapons being a waste of inventory slots (more on inventory slots in a second) but overall it's a pleasant experience with strong potential.
- the current system of missions is quite varied with multiple random events, as you fly a lot of these missions it will need more than that but it's a good start
- concept of ship being damaged and needing repairs while not new is quite fun and feels well executed
- lore is good enough for a game of this type

Now with the negatives:
- The game struggles with identity regarding progression-based gameplay and rougelite approach. It asks you to sink in hours of gameplay for very little reward yet at the same time if you fail with your party - recovery will cost you dearly as weapons that you might have been collecting through 5-10 different missions simply disappear. Re-collecting them will take ages. Having both slow, incremental progression yet at the same time harsh punishments that can erase a whole day worth of progress feel like disrespect to player's time, especially since all missions depend only on the last stage, no matter how well you've done in prior stages. Pick one: either slow grindy progression with scaling difficulty and permanent progress, or fast non-permanent progression resetting every mission, with RNG based power upgrades that all disappear on failure.
- Inventory slots are picked straight from Lethal Company-like extraction games, limited to 4 of whatever, however 1 slot is already permanent so essentially only 3 are left for the player. Given small amounts of ammunition and large amounts of enemies you usually end up taking 2 weapons extra leaving only one slot for any loot, making it really cumbersome and frustrating to play around.
- There's currently very few quests in the game, they are also all very basic.
- There’s an obvious opportunity for functional armor stats, but there's nothing there, it's just cosmetics. It feels like the devs intended to do more here but dropped it to push out Early Access.
- Rewards from mission stages are so wildly inconsistent that difficulty levels barely matter. If you get the right artifacts, Hard missions become trivial. If you get nothing useful, even Easy becomes annoying without good guns.

There’s a good game buried in here, and the core mechanics have real promise. But right now the progression, inventory system, and lack of meaningful content hold it back badly. I’ll keep an eye on development, but I can’t recommend it yet.", "voted_up": false, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 4, "timestamp_created": 1763525878}, {"review_text": "So far I am very impressed with this game. It's certainly indie as there are many things that are rough around the edges, but the overall picture is pretty clear of what the developer wants this game to be.

Being a primarily solo gamer, there is fun to be had solo at times, but this game REALLY shines in multiplayer. My buddy and I were both feeling iffy about our first couple missions alone, then we picked it up together and after one mission realized how rewarding it was to get in the swing and work together.

My main gripe is the inventory management is frustrating considering how intense missions can get. I would go into detail but I'd rather provide my opinion of a simple solution: Have a rest jump at the END of the missions, much like there's a prep jump at the start. I lost 2 Mk2 weapons(Rifle and LMG) I was hoping to hold on to for future missions but after defending a freighter I jumped automatically with the freighter and had zero time to organize inventory. 

I understand that stage in the mission wasn't about loot so it doesn't seem to be a big deal, but there were 2 loot centric missions before I hadn't really had a chance to fully sort out yet and I'm super OCD about inventory management due to games like Minecraft, Valheim, and even a little bit of extraction shooters(which this clearly takes inspiration from). A rest jump at the end of the mission would alleviate ALL of these problems. Sometimes you've got extra materia to grab a victory slice and a brew with the buds before heading back to the hangar(You could add a celebratory tone with fun stuff in crew quarters).

Gunplay and ship combat could use a little polishing, but it's got the basics down fairly well. Many of the physics don't make sense, like having fires OUTSIDE your ship in deep space. Fighting on a planet it makes more sense, but there's no consideration for physics like that. I do try to take that with a grain of salt considering it is a game and I don't expect the developer to be a physics stickler, but it would be a nice touch to work in little details like that later on.

Overall I want to applaud the developer for providing a quality game for $20. While it definitely has a long way to go, I didn't pay $70 for a game that wasn't even optimized by a studio that makes billions every year(this is my jab at wanting Borderlands 4 but refusing to buy it full price).

Jump Space should be inspiring to gamers everywhere that a game doesn't have to be perfect to be fun, or even have everything ironed out at the start. We just all need to be on the same page that the game isn't fully complete and needs work.", "voted_up": true, "votes_helpful": 0, "votes_funny": 0, "timestamp_created": 1759860832}, {"review_text": "I don't usually do these because i feel a lot of games I play dont have that much of an impact for me to feel the need to do one.

First and foremost, the devs start the volume at 50%, which is enough for a good review for me.

But this game is an absolute blast and joy to play. Whether playing solo and having Buddy help out (or even you a friend and buddy) or with a full party, this game is something else all together. It feels fantastic, your movement feels like there is some weight and significance behind it from flight or traversing inside and outside of the ship. The gun play feels good with being able to hip fire or ADS for consistent hits. Ship battles with the indicator showing you where to shoot ahead of the enemy craft so you can lead your shots correctly. Everything!

I highly recommend this game and I am super excited for more to get released, especially considering its only early access still. On the topic of early access, it feels like a complete game already, with a few things here or there that arent released yet, I havent run into any bugs or glitches yet besides maybe if your frames are buggy you can sometimes jetpack when you first get into a building.

[h3]Pros:[/h3]

+ Ship-to-foot combat is incredibly smooth. Moving around on the ship while it’s flying feels great
+ I had no performance issues. It runs really well
+ There’s some basic customization and I hope they add more options later
+ Managing the ship is fun with features like combat stations, repairs, a cool power grid system and shield repairs
+ You can craft items on board for materia
+ The guns feel satisfying to shoot
+ The grappling hook is awesome
+ You can board other ships but only from the outside
+ I love that it’s PVE with no PVP at all
+ It’s a roguelike which is cool
+ I really like that it’s also designed for solo play. I’ve heard it gets tough later on but I haven’t hit any missions yet that I couldn’t do solo
+ P2P servers mean you can still play even if the community shrinks

[h3]Cons:[/h3]

- It’s a roguelike but it suffers from the most criticized aspect of the genre: replayability. It gets repetitive really fast. Every mission feels the same no matter what you do. There are a few mission types but they all boil down to the same elements. For example a vault mission always plays out the same way with each scripted "surprise" event. It gets boring quickly.

- The enemies are way too generic and uninteresting to fight. Whether on foot or in ship combat they lack variety. The game tries to introduce different types like suicide drones and small AOE bots but they all feel the same.

- The loot isn’t rewarding enough. After fighting for 20 minutes getting just three ship repair kits feels underwhelming especially if you didn’t need them in the first place. You often have to repair your ship after almost every mission making the whole thing feel pointless. Even finishing a full run feels like an empty accomplishment. You earn some credits that don’t have any real use which is frustrating. The rewards for missions seem like an afterthought with future purchases being limited to items like ship repair kits.

- The weapons are lacking. There are a few options but most of them are pretty useless except for one that deals more damage. I don’t like when games offer a selection but make 90 percent of it obsolete.

- You’re forced to take the starting weapon with unlimited ammo which doesn’t make sense especially when playing solo with a bot companion. Your inventory is already too small and losing another slot makes it impossible to carry all the cargo from a vault mission when you also take a better weapon with you.

- The prologue which is basically the tutorial didn’t prepare me for the actual game. When I first got an artifact I was completely lost on what to do with it. I later learned that your ship gets repaired through additional missions unlocking a new room for artifact use but how was I supposed to know that.

- Every artifact which are basically ship perks felt useless to me. For example gaining 50 percent more melee damage while holding a slice of pizza is not helpful. Not only have I never ordered pizza on my ship but melee combat is never necessary. Why would I waste one of my four inventory slots on a pizza? This is even more confusing given that they announced melee weapons in the next update. Receiving these trivial artifacts felt like a slap in the face after a tough mission.

- It’s way too grindy. I hope this is just to stretch out the early access playtime until new updates arrive because you need to do a lot of bland repetitive runs to achieve anything. I’m too tired of the game to even think about grinding for another map tile.

- The ship doesn’t behave like it’s in space. You have two boosts but the ship only speeds up during the boost and immediately slows down afterward. That’s not how space works making ship-to-ship combat feel off. Maneuvering is limited. You just have to position yourself behind the enemy which makes avoiding hits feel pointless and combat in space gets repetetive. There is no strategy to it.

- I thought it was cool that you can board other ships only to find out you can just walk on their outside. Enemies spawn and you shoot them....that’s it. It is also crazy that the game encourages you more to fly freely in your spacesuit outside the ship to combat other enemy ships.

I have to say of all the games in this genre this is one of the better ones. It breaks my heart not to recommend it but I can’t because the most important aspect - interesting replayability - is missing. I got tired of this game way too quickly. A roguelike should offer more than just three mission types played in random order. It needs variety within those mission types. This game is a diamond in the rough that could be really good down the line, but right now it feels like a moon rock. [{"review_text": "I'd like to preface this by saying that I am a pilot myself, and while I don't know everything, I can speak to a few aspects of the simulator.

Firstly, there are many positive aspects to the sim. The world is recreated in amazing detail, the overall game is gorgeous, and while the airplane flight feel isn't as good as X-Plane, the aircraft are lovingly and even lavishly recreated. MSFS 2024 can legitimately be used as a training tool for a number of aircraft systems at this point.

Unfortunately, that is where my compliments must end. Despite being in the United States and using a 150 Mbps connection, the game constantly tells me my connection is too slow. I have traced the problem to MSFS`s content delivery network, which despite having had weeks to improve, is only pushing data to me at about 7 Mbps. That is the best that can be done with a VPN to several major server farms. Without the VPN, I'm lucky to get more than 4 Mbps. Loading and transitioning is agonizingly slow, prone to crashing, and often loads textures and models so blurred they would fit better into Flight Simulator 98 than anything modern. And yes, this often includes the cockpits! You can start a flight with a modern cockpit, look at some nicely rendered scenery in exterior view, and then return to cockpit view and time travel to 1998 graphics. There is no guarantee the rendering will fix itself, BTW.

And that extends to Career Mode as well, which can charitably called unfair. Sometimes you will get dinged for taxi-overspeeding for crawling along at 2 kts. A gust of wind causes your 172 to hit 86 kts, and immediately you get dinged for flap overspeed. The sim perpetually proposes nonsensical flight routes, and the ATC simulation sometimes croaks without allowing any of the inputs to continue dialog. The game teleports the taxi route you are following right before your eyes and then immediately spanks you for being outside of the expected taxi area. The game will happily arrange your fixed wing flights to include "runways" that would make a helicopter nervous. It will also occasionally spawn invisible walls, or trees in your taxi route, or cars fixed into the middle of runways. I run it on an aging 2021 rig (i9-11900K / RTX3080) with triple screens 3k (3x 1920x1080 at 60 degrees) resolution, which works well btw. In the beginning I struggled to get more than 30fps with blurry graphics and occasional weird graphical clippings at the edge of airports, looked nothing like the screenshots, weird looking houses and trees. Now I have crisp graphics running at 60fps and going down to 40fps on busy airports. So, getting this game to run on your hardware (and looking nice) may require some effort to say the least, if you don’t own the latest generation top rig.
 
The career mode, which was the main reason for getting this is very addictive for me. I don’t seem to have the many bugs others are experiencing. I enjoy the slow pace of it. Basically, you start of without your own plane making like 2k per mission. Once you rack up like 30k you can buy a Cessna 172, making like 150k per mission, next step may be a used Cessna Caravan costing like 3mil, which makes you like 500k-1mil per mission, and so on. I’m 80 missions in and own my fourth plane (cost 8mil and making 1-2mil per mission) saving up for a jet (at 32mil). The bugs people are talking mainly relate to the weird blue boxes the sim wants you to fly through. Forget those, I have turned them off, you don’t need to follow them, you only need to stop short of runway at blue box, go through assigned waypoints (in IFR flight) and enter correct final on assigned runway, then stop short of taxi when landed (blue box) and then park at assigned location (blue box). You do not need to follow the markers, they are borked and takes away immersion anyway. Btw, you can use accelerated time in career mode (with full payout) or just skip the whole flight once you have reached cruising altitude (but then your payout is lower).
